detail: From the two SP-016 security reviews, accepted as Low or informational: (1) a process reparented out of the harness tree (launchd, open, osascript) counts as the operator, as documented under Caller sessions; reading the command log makes that bypass more rewarding, and the OS sandbox (SP-046) is the boundary; (2) a session that runs 'orch spaces log' puts its own redacted log into its transcript, which the session-end summary ingests into RAG; the text is the session's own commands, already in its transcript, but decide whether INV-12 should refuse the table inside a harness; (3) 'orch spaces log verify' prints the owner and problem details without cell(); (4) the CLI buffers every page and shares one 30 s deadline, so a very large log can time out having printed nothing (flush per page or stream); (5) the shared flush is best effort (a reader joining a running flush may miss events taken just before it called); (6) the summary's placing deadline cannot interrupt a stat that blocks (an autofs or dead network mount under /net or /Volumes); consider skipping non-local filesystems. (7) no test pins grpc.MaxConcurrentStreams in newGRPCServer, so a refactor could drop it silently; (8) two 'orch spaces log' runs from one session at the same moment: the second is refused (ResourceExhausted) with no retry.
